findings.summary: Logical inconsistency in Verification Plan for R3 (Markdown Parsing). Milestone M2 claims to pass Acceptance Test AT3 (a system test requiring inspection of generated HTML pages), but the component responsible for writing pages to the output directory (Emit Plugin, DL25) is not scheduled for delivery until Milestone M6.

evidence.note: M2 claims AT3 passes (one-to-one HTML page generation).
evidence.quote: AT3 (one-to-one HTML page generation for non-excluded files) passes.

evidence.note: Emit Plugin (writing pages to output) is delivered in M6.
evidence.quote: Emit Plugin (C17) writing all pages and assets to output directory...

evidence.note: AT3 is a System test implying output inspection.

findings.summary: Verification of Requirement R1 (Recursive Discovery) is deferred to Milestone M6 (AT1), despite the implementing component (Ingestion Plugin, DL4) being delivered in Milestone M1. This creates a verification gap where core ingestion functionality is not formally accepted until the final assembly stage.

evidence.note: Ingestion Plugin deliverable in M1 satisfies R1.
evidence.quote: Skeleton Ingestion Plugin (C11) that scans a directory and populates the build context with raw note entries (satisfies R1 partially).

evidence.note: M6 Exit Criteria includes AT1.
M1 Exit Criteria excludes AT1.

findings.summary: Sample check for R1 maps work to milestones M1 and M2, but the plan places the end-to-end recursive discovery acceptance test (AT1) in M6 exit criteria; M2 does not mention R1/AT1 deliverables, so the trace mapping appears incorrect.

evidence.note: Deterministic sample check claims R1 is covered by M1 and M2.
M6 exit criteria includes AT1 (recursive Markdown discovery) as an end-to-end check.
M2 deliverables are focused on Markdown rendering/XSS; no mention of recursive discovery acceptance (AT1).

findings.summary: Sample check for R2 maps work to milestones M1 and M2, but the plan positions the static-output acceptance test (AT2) in M6 exit criteria; M1/M2 do not list emit/site assembly deliverables needed to satisfy AT2, indicating trace mismatch.

evidence.note: Deterministic sample check claims R2 is covered by M1 and M2.
M6 exit criteria includes AT2 (purely static output, loads without server runtime).
evidence.quote: AT2 (output is purely static, loads without server runtime) passes.

evidence.note: Emit Plugin (C17) that writes pages/assets appears in M6, aligning more directly with AT2 than M1/M2.
evidence.quote: Emit Plugin (C17) writing all pages and assets to output directory with configurable base URL/path prefix (R19).

findings.summary: Sample check for R3 maps to M1 and M2 with AT3, but the plan’s M2 exit criteria requires AT3 (one-to-one HTML page generation) even though page templating and emitting are planned for M6; this creates an internal trace inconsistency about when HTML pages actually get generated.

evidence.note: Deterministic sample check claims R3 is covered by M1 and M2.
M2 exit criteria claims AT3 passes (HTML page generation).
evidence.quote: AT3 (one-to-one HTML page generation for non-excluded files) passes.

evidence.note: Theme/Template Plugin (C15) rendering per-note pages is planned for M6.
evidence.quote: Theme/Template Plugin (C15) rendering per-note pages with tags, backlinks, and search UI.

evidence.note: Emit Plugin (C17) that writes pages/assets is planned for M6, suggesting HTML outputs are assembled/emitted there rather than in M2.
evidence.quote: Emit Plugin (C17) writing all pages and assets to output directory with configurable base URL/path prefix (R19).
